adjudication.rationale: In `packages/core/EventManager.ts` `createAllCalendarEvents`, the loop calls `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)` for each `destination` entry, and `CalendarManager.createEvent` returns that passed `externalId` on the `EventResult`. However, several calendar service implementations shown in the diff ignore the per-destination `externalId` and instead always target the first destination calendar entry: e.g. Lark/Office365/BaseCalendarService all do `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []; const calendarId = mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId;`. That means when `event.destinationCalendar` contains multiple entries, an event may be created in `event.destinationCalendar[0]` while the stored reference/result records `destination.externalId` for a different entry, causing later update/delete operations to potentially use the wrong calendar ID.
